Git Locator: The inline code `<path>@<commit>` naming a removed file at a commit that holds it and that the default branch or a tag reaches, written in place of a link to that file. When no such commit exists it names the path and the record's pull request ([ADR-0278](docs/adr/0278-a-retirement-deletes-and-the-history-root-holds-only-archive-records.md)).
History Root: The single repository directory holding only Archive Records; Git keeps the full text of removed material. It is resolved in one place so every consumer uses the same root ([ADR-0278](docs/adr/0278-a-retirement-deletes-and-the-history-root-holds-only-archive-records.md)).
History Sanitize Command: The `roundfix history sanitize` command, a dry run unless `--apply --batch <n>`, that converts Legacy Archive Folders to Archive Records, removes retired families and rewrites their citations to Git Locators after the History Full Tag. `roundfix baseline update` runs the same planning for all eligible units at once ([ADR-0278](docs/adr/0278-a-retirement-deletes-and-the-history-root-holds-only-archive-records.md)).
Reduced History Entry: A legacy shape of a retired Finding or Backlog Entry containing its front matter, title, first paragraph and the revision holding its full text. The History Sanitize Command removes it; no retirement writes one ([ADR-0278](docs/adr/0278-a-retirement-deletes-and-the-history-root-holds-only-archive-records.md)).
Rollup: A Finding of `rollup` kind that consolidates related Findings as declared members and retires by deletion when its work is resolved. Its members resolve as unresolved Findings or through Git, which keeps their retired text ([ADR-0278](docs/adr/0278-a-retirement-deletes-and-the-history-root-holds-only-archive-records.md)).
Backlog Entry: Typed intent for what to do next, with a lifecycle of `open`, `promoted` to a named Spec, or a terminal status (`declined`, `deferred`, `done`, `deprecated`, `superseded`, `closed` or `cancelled`); a terminal entry is deleted and Git keeps its text, while `declined` and `deferred` carry a reason ([ADR-0278](docs/adr/0278-a-retirement-deletes-and-the-history-root-holds-only-archive-records.md)). Its types express intent through the Conventional Commits vocabulary — `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor` — and it is never evidence; a `feat` entry is upstream raw material, never the `write-idea` artifact.
Legacy Link Rebase: The rewrite of relative destinations in an Archive Record outcome and each promoted copy: a folder destination points at its promoted copy, or becomes a Git Locator when no copy survives, never the record itself; every other destination keeps the same repository path ([ADR-0278](docs/adr/0278-a-retirement-deletes-and-the-history-root-holds-only-archive-records.md)).
History Relocation: One file carried in the Baseline Plan as an ordered ledger entry of source, destination and content identity, never into the Findings, Backlog, ADR or Review families of the History Root. An occupied destination refuses that relocation by name while its siblings still move ([ADR-0278](docs/adr/0278-a-retirement-deletes-and-the-history-root-holds-only-archive-records.md)).
History Citation: A citation to a file or folder a selected history unit removes, listed in text and JSON and bound into the Plan Digest. In Archive Records, Live Documents and the user guide it is rewritten to a Git Locator for removed text, or to the surviving record or promoted copy when one exists ([ADR-0278](docs/adr/0278-a-retirement-deletes-and-the-history-root-holds-only-archive-records.md)).
